subject: chemistry
question_text: Write the van der Waals equation.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The equation
lines: For n moles of a real gas.
a corrects the pressure for intermolecular attraction;
b corrects the volume for the space the molecules
steps.why: A real gas needs two corrections to PV = nRT: measured pressure is lower than ideal because molecules attract one another (the an²/V² term), and the free volume is smaller than the vessel because molecules have size (the nb term).
common_mistakes: Writing (P − an²/V²). The correction is ADDED to the measured pressure.
Writing (V + nb). The correction is SUBTRACTED from the vessel volume.
Dropping the n² and n on the two corrections for n moles.
steps.memory_tip: Plus on pressure, minus on volume: attraction lowered the pressure, so add it back; molecular size removed free volume, so subtract it.
steps.margin_note: One line of equation with the signs right earns the mark; the two correction sentences show the meaning.

steps.label: Units of a and b
lines: Units of a: atm L² mol⁻²
steps.why: an²/V² must carry pressure units, so a carries atm L² mol⁻²; nb must carry volume units, so b carries L mol⁻¹. The units follow from the equation instead of being memorised separately.
common_mistakes: Swapping the units of a and b.
Writing a in atm L mol⁻¹ — the volume in a's unit is squared.
steps.memory_tip: a sits in the pressure bracket, so its unit is pressure × volume² per mole². b is a volume per mole.
steps.margin_note: In SI the same units read Pa m⁶ mol⁻² and m³ mol⁻¹; the atm–litre forms are the expected ones.

insider_note: Both halves are marked: 1 mark for the equation and 1 mark for the units of a and b, so write both. Inside the equation the two signs are what examiners check first — plus inside the pressure bracket, minus inside the volume bracket.
